post.description:
Mail a sign-in code to an address.

The answer is the same whether or not that address has an account, so
nobody can ask this endpoint who is registered.

Spend a code, and answer with the session cookie every route wants.

The User is created here when the address is new to the instance.
End this session. The cookie that carried it stops working at once.

get.description:
The signed-in User, and the Workspaces they are a member of.

The list is empty for someone signing in for the first time, which is the
signal the editor lands them on Workspace creation with.

post.description: Create a Workspace with its Owner and bundled fonts ready to use.

patch.description: Give the Workspace another name. Only an Owner may.

delete.description:
Delete the Workspace and its contents. Only an Owner may, and it ends
the Workspace for every member of it at once.

get.description: Everyone in the Workspace. Any member may see who they work with.

patch.description: Give one member a different Role. Only an Owner may.

delete.description: Take somebody out of the Workspace. Only an Owner may.

post.description: Give up your own Membership. Every member may, the last Owner aside.
Create a design in this Workspace, at revision one.

get.description:
This Workspace's documents, newest change first, without their bodies.

The whole list, every time: a Workspace holds the documents one team
authors by hand, which is a number a person scrolls.
One document, whole. Any member of its Workspace may read it.

put.description:
Store a new version of a document against the Revision it was loaded at.

The Revision is checked by the write itself rather than before it, so two
saves that arrive together cannot both find the revision they expect.

delete.description:
Delete a document.

A template promoted from it stands on its own — it holds a copy, not a
reference — and loses only the lineage back to what is gone.

post.description:
Copy a design into a new template, and answer with the copy.

A copy, not a reference: from this moment the template and the design it
came from change without each other, which is the whole point of
promoting one.

Turn this document into a file. Editor-level; a Viewer is refused.

The bytes come back on this response. The same call twice is two
responses; nothing is recorded and nothing is stored.

Take a font file into this Workspace. Editor-level; a Viewer is refused.

Answers 201 with the new record, or 200 with the record this Workspace
already held for these bytes — a re-upload is a no-op by construction, and
the editor never has to explain a duplicate.

422.description: The file is not an asset this product takes.

get.description:
This Workspace's Font Assets, newest first.

The whole library, every time: a Workspace holds the faces one team
uploaded, which is a number a picker scrolls.
The font's own bytes. Any member of its Workspace may fetch them.

delete.description:
Delete a font. Editor-level; a Viewer is refused.

Unconditionally, and without counting anything (ADR-0007): a design, a
template or an in-flight Generation Job that referenced it fails loudly by
the missing-asset rule, and re-uploading the same bytes revives every one
of those references at the same id.

The row goes first and the object second. The other order would leave a
record of a font whose bytes are gone, which is a font that cannot be
served; this one leaves bytes nothing points at, which cost nothing.

409.description: The asset is one this product does not let go of.

422.description: The file is not an asset this product takes.

This Workspace's Image Assets, newest first.

The whole library, every time: a Workspace holds the pictures one team

The image's own bytes. Any member of its Workspace may fetch them.

The row goes first and the object second. The other order would leave a

post.description:
Submit a batch against this Template, or return the Job a repeated
idempotency key already created.

A text/csv body is the same channel: format and idempotency key travel
as query parameters, cells stay strings, and the worker types them.

get.description: One Job, with every Row and the counts taken from those Rows.
One succeeded Row's file, streamed from the api's own storage.
Every succeeded Row, as one zip, streamed rather than assembled.

This Workspace's Jobs, newest first, without per-Row detail.

The whole list, every time: a Workspace holds the batches one team
submits, which is a number a person scrolls.

AssetRefusalView.title: AssetRefusalView
AssetRefusalView.description: The body of every asset refusal, whatever status carries it.

BatchRefusal.title: BatchRefusal
BatchRefusal.description: What a refused batch answers with: one error per problem.

DocumentKind.title: DocumentKind
DocumentKind.description:
Which of the two things a stored document is.

One table holds both, so opening one is a single code path; this column is
the only thing that tells them apart. A design becomes a template by being
copied into one, never by changing this value.

DocumentSummary.title: DocumentSummary
DocumentSummary.description: A stored document without the document — what one list row carries.

FontAssetView.title: FontAssetView
FontAssetView.description: One Font Asset, as the editor's picker and Assets panel read it.

FontFormat.title: FontFormat
FontFormat.description: The two file formats a Font Asset is ever stored as.

ImageAssetView.title: ImageAssetView
ImageAssetView.description: One Image Asset, as the editor's Assets panel and canvas read it.

JobState.title: JobState
JobState.description:
Where a Generation Job is, as a whole.

`completed` covers runs that had per-Row failures; the Rows carry the
detail. `queued` is where a Job starts, and where it stays until a Row
begins rendering — that flip belongs to the internal fetch (4dpprd).

JobSummary.title: JobSummary
JobSummary.description:
A Job as the Workspace list shows it: no per-Row detail, and the
Template's name joined in.

MemberView.title: MemberView
MemberView.description: A User in one Workspace, from the Workspace's side.

MembershipView.title: MembershipView
MembershipView.description: A Workspace one User is in, from that User's side.

NamedProblem.title: NamedProblem
NamedProblem.description: One problem the worker found: a message, and the thing at fault.

NewDocument.title: NewDocument
NewDocument.description: What creating takes. Only a design: promotion is the door to a template.

Refusal.title: Refusal
Refusal.description:
Why a file was refused: the code the editor branches on, and the
sentence it shows when it has nothing better.

RenderBody.title: RenderBody
RenderBody.description: What rendering takes: the values, and the file they should become.

RenderRefusal.title: RenderRefusal
RenderRefusal.description: What POST /render answers when the values are wrong.

Role.title: Role
Role.description:
What one Membership may do inside its Workspace.

The v1 set is closed, and the declaration order is the ladder: each Role
covers everything the ones above it in this list may do, which is what
lets a route name the least Role that is enough for it.

RowError.title: RowError
RowError.description: A NamedProblem that also says which Row it is in.

RowStatus.title: RowStatus
RowStatus.description: Where one Row of a Generation Job is.

RowView.title: RowView
RowView.description:
One Row as polling shows it. `error` and `url` stay off the wire
until the Row has one.

Save.title: Save
Save.description: What saving takes, including the Revision the caller loaded.

Saved.title: Saved
Saved.description: What a save answers with: the revision it produced, and when.
